chunks: Aban ibn Uthman from Uqba that he heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying:

Indeed, when the soul of a man reaches his chest, he sees. I said, 'May I be sacrificed for you, and what does he see?' He said, 'He sees the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), and the Messenger of Allah says to him: I am the Messenger of Allah, receive glad tidings.' Then he sees Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him), and he says: I am Ali ibn Abi Talib, whom you used to love. Your love will benefit you today.
He said, I said to him, 'Can it be that one of the people sees this and then returns to the world?' He said, 'No. When he sees this, he dies forever, and that is a great thing.'

And that is in the Quran, the Word of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic: 'Those who believed and were righteous. For them is good news in the life of the world and in the Hereafter; there is no changing the Words of Allah.'
ai.seo_question: What does a believer see at the moment of death according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) describes the visionary experience of a believer at the moment of death, where the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) and Imam Ali (AS) appear to offer glad tidings based on the believer's love for them. The Imam clarifies that this vision is not a temporary trance but a permanent state leading to death, linking it to the concept of 'Bashara' (good news) in the Hereafter. This highlights the Shia theological emphasis on the intercessory role of the Ahl al-Bayt and the spiritual reality of the soul's transition.

en.hubeali:
Aban Bin Usman, 
(It has been narrated) from Uqba who heard Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> saying:

‘The man, when his soul comes up to be in his chest, sees’. I said, ‘May I be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>! And what does he see?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘He sees Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>, and Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> is saying to him: ‘Receive glad tidings!’ The he sees Ali<sup>asws</sup> Bin Abu Talib<sup>asws</sup>, and he<sup>asws</sup> is saying to him: ‘I<sup>asws</sup> am Ali<sup>asws</sup> Bin Abu Talib<sup>asws</sup>, whom you used to love. Your love would benefit you today’.

He (the narrator) said, ‘I said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘Can it happen for anyone from the people when he sees this, then he would return to the world?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘No. When he sees this, he would be dead forever, and that is a great thing.
And that is in the Quran, the Words of Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic [10:64] For them is good news in the life of the world and in the Hereafter; there is no changing the Words of Allah’.
en.sarwar: 8. Aban ibn ‘Uthman has narrated from ‘Uqbah who had heard abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, saying the following:

“I heard abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, say, ‘When a man’s soul reaches his chest he then sees.’ I then asked, ‘May Allah keep my soul in the service of your cause, what does he see?’ The Imam said, ‘He sees the Messenger of Allah and he says, “I am the Messenger of Allah. I have good news for you.” He then sees Ali ibn abu Talib, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, who says, “I am Ali ibn abu Talib, whom you loved. He loves to benefit you today.’”
I then asked, ‘Can anyone who sees them come back to this life?’ He said, ‘No, when one sees them, he then can never return back to this life.’ He considered it a great thing.

He said this is in the Quran in the words of Allah, the Majestic, the Glorious, ‘Those who believe, who were faithful to their belief, receive good news in this world and in the next life and there is no change in the words of Allah.’” [10:64]
